title: Mourners call for killing of young black men to end; Man, 26, shot by police died in 'senseless' way Last October, victim reported hearing voices: [ONT Edition]
article: As grieving family and friends gathered at the funeral of O'Brien Christopher\-Reid, an angry and mournful plea echoed through the chapel calling for an end to the violent deaths of young black men.

Christopher-Reid, 26, was shot June 13 on a footpath near Wilket Creek Park by three police officers who had been called after people reported seeing an emotionally disturbed young man carrying a knife.

"A prince has fallen in Scarborough," said Rev. Ransford Jones, youth pastor at the Agincourt Church of God, who gave the sermon at yesterday's service at the Rosewood Church of the Nazarene in Scarborough.
"Another black man has died by a bullet. Too many of our young men are being killed by the gun. Whether it's by legal or illegal guns, this must stop."
Rev. Delton Fraser, uncle to Christopher-Reid, told the 500 mourners that "our grief is magnified because of the senseless and violent way O'Brien died and was shot."

Family and friends celebrated Christopher-Reid's life in a two- hour service, extolling his virtues his devotion to his family and friends, his intelligence and his love of cooking. They spoke of his first years growing up in Jamaica and his participation in the Agincourt Church's youth choir and drama program.
His mother, Jacqueline Christopher, surrounded by family and friends, broke down as her son's casket was carried into the hearse.
Last October, Christopher-Reid had been hospitalized for three days, according to a statement from a family member.

At the time he told his mother he was hearing voices and felt people were out to get him, said Ian Daley, a lawyer who is married to a cousin of Christopher-Reid. "The doctors informed Jacqueline that he wasn't posing any threat to himself or to others and he was released."

Then in January, 2004, Christopher-Reid checked himself back into the same hospital for a psychiatric assessment. He was there for a week and then checked himself out. The family was not aware of any diagnosis, Daley said.
Jacqueline Christopher and her ex-husband, Earle Reid, are hoping the Special Investigations Unit will piece together what happened to their son.
